To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unconscious visual processing is not automatic but is attentionally controlled.
unconscious visual processing depends on attention.
attentional sensitization of subliminal prim ing depends on attentional control processes, stimulus expectations, action intentions, and task sets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how attentional top down influences modulate automatic processes in general and subliminal prim ing in particular.
the role of top down attentional control for automatic processing.
the nature of the relationship between attention and unconscious processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

unconscious perception is not automatic in the sense of being autonomous and independent of top down influences, but that it depends on the cognitive system being configured in such a way that the unconscious processing pathways are amplified and facilitated.
the attentional sensitization of automatic processes is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by many different variables.
attentional sensitization is a necessary prerequisite for unconscious visual processing and, hence, attention and unconscious processing are inseparably linked.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attention is a necessary condition of unconscious processing.
attentional sensitization is a powerful and ubiquitous mechanism that can account for many previously puzzling phenomena in cognitive psychology.
attentional sensitization is the key to understanding the nature of automaticity in the human mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automaticity of unconscious visual processing is a function of the attentional configuration of the cognitive system.
the distinction between automatic and controlled processing is not a fundamental one.
attention is not only required to process conscious information but is also necessary for unconscious visual processing.
